extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2020 paper reviewers (and authors preparing broader impact statements)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers (and corresponding author guidance) on evaluating the NeurIPS 2020 Broader Impact statement, including what authors must include, what reviewers should check for, and acceptable mitigation or 'not applicable' responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact statement (author requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were required to include a statement of the potential broader impact of their work, including: ethical aspects, future societal consequences, and both positive and negative outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should discuss potential negative societal impacts if appropriate. Authors could also state that a broader impact discussion was not applicable if the work was very theoretical or general enough with no particular application foreseen. This requirement existed in 2020 and later evolved into checklist items used in subsequent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer question: adequacy of broader impact discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Have the authors adequately addressed the broader impact of their work, including potential negative ethical and societal implications of their work?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers were explicitly asked to answer this question when evaluating submissions that included a broader impact statement. The question is evaluative: reviewers should judge whether the authors have meaningfully considered and explained broader impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the submission raised potential ethical concerns, including methods, applications, or data that: create or reinforce unfair bias; have a primary purpose of harm or injury; use sensitive personal data without proper consent; have national security implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider and report these specific categories of concern when present. The guideline lists these as examples of the kinds of ethical issues to look for in methods, applications, or data choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation strategies for negative impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors could discuss mitigation strategies for potential negative societal impacts, such as gated release of models, providing defenses, and mechanisms for monitoring misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When negative impacts are plausible, authors are encouraged to propose concrete mitigation measures (e.g., withholding full model release, providing defensive techniques, or monitoring/alerting mechanisms). Reviewers should evaluate whether proposed mitigations are reasonable and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible 'not applicable' claim for theoretical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were free to write that a broader impact discussion was not applicable if their work was very theoretical or general enough with no particular application foreseen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A succinct statement that broader impacts are not applicable is acceptable for sufficiently theoretical work; reviewers should accept such claims when justified by lack of foreseeable application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy: Paper checklist items on Broader Impacts and Safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2020 broader impact requirement later evolved into the NeurIPS Paper Checklist (specifically items 10 and 11 on Broader Impacts and Safeguards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principles from the 2020 requirement were carried forward into checklist-style items used across ML conferences; reviewers and authors may now encounter these as checklist questions rather than free-form mandatory statements.
